name: W. Graham Robertson
bio: Artist, illustrator and stage designer (1866-1948), painted by Sargent in 1894 and the owner of an important collection of Blake drawings. His children's play Pinkie and the Fairies was produced by Tree in 1908, and his autobiography Time Was (1931) is a standard source for the period. He was twenty-one when Wilde began writing to him in 1887 and Wilde was thirty-three. Seven of Wilde's letters to him survive, running to 1893, and they are among the most affectionate he wrote to anyone outside the circle this map already draws: 'your narcissus keeps you in my memory'; 'You are made for olive-groves, and for meadows starred with white narcissi'; 'I should have loved to have been with you'. He bought Wilde a drawing of Sarah Bernhardt, illustrated for him, and paid Charles Ricketts, of whom Wilde's first recorded impression is in a letter to Robertson.
bio_note: Seven letters at PDF 359, 369 (two on one page), 412, 420, 432 and 612; five have been read at the page (printed 347, 390, 398, 410, and the two at 347), every folio confirmed on its own page image. Two remain located but unread: PDF 359 (postmark 12 December 1887, the earliest) and 612 (postmark 14 April 1893, sending a first-night stall). Dates: none recorded — the editors give none on the pages read, and none is inferred.
